description:
## Why
A streaming fleet freezes when teardown joins a reader blocked on a full Ghostty mailbox, and large sends arrive truncated or with a reply inside the paste. One submodule patch set closes those doors. Backlog items: B065, B010 (Ghostty half), B031, B013, B047, B072, B204, B062, B022, plus the 2026-08-25 freeze.

## Evidence
Citations are origin/main `0ff8887e5e` and Ghostty `26c3e499e`. Re-find every line before editing. C11-248 renamed panel/surface to tab, and the ledger's lines are stale.

- B065: `ghostty/src/App.zig:239` drains with `while (self.mailbox.pop())` and does not bound the turn or re-wake.
- B010, corrected by Astra: `ghostty/src/termio/stream_handler.zig:131-134` unlocks `renderer_state.mutex` before the blocking app-mailbox push. The autosave mutex cycle as first filed is not the deadlock. The recorded cycle is main freeing a surface while a reader is parked on that mailbox. App free sites: `Sources/GhosttyTerminalView.swift` (the `Task { @MainActor in ghostty_surface_free(...) }` paths near 3287 and 4328). Writeup: `notes/2026-08-25-freeze-surface-deinit-deadlock.md`. The Ghostty half is teardown-abortable producer pushes, not a bigger queue and not an autosave lock dance.
- B031: `ghostty/src/Surface.zig:3336` and `:3352` push visibility and focus with `.forever`. The renderer queue is not the app queue. Display-id already uses a nonblocking push (C11-200). Do not revert it.
- Fable: eighteen `.forever` pushes in `Surface.zig` (927, 944, 1449, 1467, 1482, 1506, 1510, 1800, 2471, 3336, 3352, 5394, 5406, 5971, and the app-mailbox sites). Change the push policy. Patching two call sites leaves the other doors.
- B013: `completeClipboardPaste` queues one IO message per vector, so the bracket fence, the payload, and the closing fence are three messages. A terminal reply can land between them. Upstream Ghostty `f27772d10`.
- B047: `ghostty/src/datastruct/segmented_pool.zig` advances availability without recording which slot returned. Wrong-order reuse can corrupt an outstanding write. Astra: `put()` does not literally refuse an out-of-order return. No c11 byte-loss count was measured. Upstream `e0ef934f7` pools the request and the buffer together.
- B072, probable: the pinned libxev stream watcher drops a queued write on every error, including WouldBlock. Establish that this backend actually surfaces WouldBlock before changing it. An explicit disproof retires the row.
- B204: `ghostty/src/Surface.zig` `setSelection` saves the previous selection, calls `select`, then compares with `sel.eql(prev)` after `select` has released those pins. Upstream `ab82b8ab7`. Describe it as a lifetime bug. Do not add a gesture recipe.
- B062: `ghostty/src/termio/Exec.zig` loops `killpg(SIGHUP)` then `waitpid(WNOHANG)` and sleeps 10 ms, with no deadline and no escalation.
- B022: shutdown treats the direct child exiting as done and does not track the foreground group, so descendants survive. Port with the later safety constraints (`bc7e9f746`), not the stale cached-PGID design.
- Research: `upstream-triage/c11-1.0/05-bug-sweep-data/audit-fable.md` §3–§5 cluster C1 and C3, wave 2. `audit-astra.md` §2 (B010 overturn) and §4 cluster 1. Tiers approved in `05-bug-reconciled.md` on 2026-10-01.

## Scope
In: one Ghostty patch set on the current c11 fork (`26c3e499e`), pushed to `Stage-11-Agentics/ghostty` before the parent pointer moves.
- Bound the app-mailbox drain and re-wake so a leftover message still runs (B065). Upstream `2258bea96`, renderer `188d31a97`.
- Producer waits that teardown joins become abortable, including the renderer-first teardown path (B010 Ghostty half, the 08-25 root). A larger mailbox alone does not break the cycle.
- Focus and visibility publish the latest value without parking. Never drop the final visible or focused state (B031). Upstream `ca21db1bb`. Do not use a push that can discard the last update.
- One owned paste message (B013).
- Write-pool ownership that survives out-of-order completion (B047).
- WouldBlock only if the trigger is real on this backend (B072).
- Selection comparison that does not read a released pin (B204).
- Bounded child shutdown, then escalation, without killing a process the operator meant to keep (B062, B022).

Ride-alongs, same bump, fix in this PR when the cherry-pick is clean: B021 (dead PTY spin and reaping), B015 (row-boundary column), B020 (zero-capacity compact loop), B034 (grapheme widen at the right edge), B036 (hyperlink reflow shape), B037 (preedit glyph bounds), B045 (null font name), B166 (shaped-cell index). Skip a ride-along that does not apply, and say so in the PR.

Out:
- The app half of B010, screen-read formatting, and cold-start adoption. Those are the app ticket, which depends on this bump.
- C11-227, the full rebase onto cmux's Ghostty base. Do not wait for it. If it lands first, drop any commit already in the new base.
- C11-200's display-id push.
- An upstream Ghostty PR as a merge gate. D23 is out of 1.0. Leave the operator a one-line note. Do not block.
- Parked engine rows, re-check only while you are in the file: B026, B039, B041, B052, B053, B054, B055, B057, B063, B121, B139, B171.
- IME, clipboard, and non-US input rows. They are named on the send-key ticket.

## Approach
One fork branch, one checksum cycle. Cherry-pick the named commits where they apply. Where c11 has diverged, port the invariant, not the diff. Push the submodule to `stage11` before updating the parent gitlink. `scripts/ghosttykit-checksums.txt` is filled by `build-ghosttykit`, not by hand. Run 1 of that workflow goes red until the Zig build finishes. That red is expected. `GHOSTTY_RELEASE_TOKEN` is not set on this fork. Publish any xcframework with `--prerelease --latest=false` so it cannot take Sparkle's latest slot.

Keep tick behavior boring: a bounded drain must still wake again, or input stalls until the next unrelated message. Latest-value publication stores the newest focus and visibility and the renderer applies that value. It does not drop updates on the floor.

Child shutdown gets a deadline, then a stronger signal, and it must not reap a process group the operator kept on purpose. The prompt-escalation note in the B062 ledger row is the guidance.

B033 (off-main scrollbar and color callbacks in `GhosttyTerminalView.swift`) is the app coalescing ticket. If this bump moves those callbacks off the app mailbox, say so in the PR so that ticket still hops to main.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A fixture or Ghostty test fills the app mailbox and frees the surface from the app side. The free returns. The process stays up. This is the 2026-08-25 shape, not a new hang class.
2. With 30 panes printing continuously, a keystroke still reaches the focused terminal. The app tick does not run until the mailbox is empty when producers keep filling it. A message left after the bound is still processed.
3. Focus and occlusion of a background workspace still settle on the last requested state. Hiding and then showing a workspace ends visible. A full renderer mailbox does not park main.
4. `c11 send` of a multi-line brief into a Claude Code or Codex tab arrives as one bracketed paste. A terminal reply does not sit between the fences. A large send is not missing a chunk. If B072 is disproved, the PR says why WouldBlock is not reachable.
5. Copy-on-select in a terminal does not crash the app across a few seconds of selection changes.
6. Closing a tab whose child ignores SIGHUP returns within the deadline. A descendant the shutdown is supposed to reap is gone. A process the operator kept is still running. State the keep rule in the PR.

## Validation
Ghostty unit tests for the commits that have them. Then a tagged c11 build. Builds and the soak run on Atlas once C11-216 lands. The soak is C11-270: 30 streaming panes, surface create and close every few seconds, autosave on, and one child that ignores SIGHUP. Record typing latency before and after. Do not run `xcodebuild` on Hyperion. No app-level display link and no manual `ghostty_surface_draw` loop.

## Dependencies
Blocks the app-half ticket (B010 app half, B086, B003). Coordinate with the wakeup-coalescing ticket so tick changes are not stacked blind. Cross-workstream: F1 is C11-216 (builds), F2 is C11-270 (soak). The lead links those. C11-227 is related, not a prerequisite.

## Risks
Typing latency: a bounded drain changes tick cadence. Measure it. Deadlock: an abort that loses the last visibility update, or a shutdown that escalates too wide, is a new incident. Submodule: never commit the parent pointer before the fork push. Checksum: do not hand-edit the pin. Public repo: lifetime and shutdown bugs, no trigger recipe beyond the fixture above. No new UI strings. Doctrine: Ghostty-only. No tenant config writes.

Size: L. Tier: P0. Doctrine check: the patch set stays inside the Ghostty fork and the parent gitlink.
title: Make Ghostty mailbox waits abortable and ship the 1.0 terminal patch set
